To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the children’s perception of leisure time in the SFO 1 is a mixture of the official and the unofficial life, and a mixture of play and dialogue.
children’s perceptions of SFO are ambiguous.
the children’s leisure time is a mixture of fun and boredom, of freedom and control, of play and work.
In summary, our research is concerned with

children’s perceptions of the institutional framework of the school day‐ care centre and how this framework influences children’s perceptions of leisure and play. 3 The empirical study is based on a series of interviews with children in two different SFOs in Oslo, Norway.
the question of how children’s perceptions of leisure time and play can be understood and interpreted in the context of the official and unofficial worlds in which they live.
children’s perceptions of time and leisure in the institutional framework of the SFO.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the children’s leisure time is not a separate entity from their everyday life.
children’s play and leisure time is a complex and ambiguous phenomenon.
the carnival is a central element of the children’s unofficial life in the SFO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

children’s perceptions of leisure time and play are closely connected to the institutionalised world of school and SFO. 3 The children’s perceptions of play and leisure time can be seen as the opposite of their perceptions of the institutionalised world.
children’s leisure is a carnival of life.
children’s play and leisure time in SFO is not only about fun and amusement, it is about children’s own interpretations and negotiations of what is important to them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children have their own perceptions of leisure time, which are not necessarily the same as the adult’s.
children are not passive victims of institutionalisation but rather active and creative agents in the construction of their own leisure time.
we need to be aware that leisure is a concept that can be used to understand children’s lives, and that children’s leisure time is an area that needs to be taken seriously in research.
